searchText: The research group's methodology is fundamentally flawed They assume that 1 validator equates to 1 node, whereas 1 validator in the becon chain protocol just represents 32 eth in the consensus and many validators are often run on a single node through empirical analysis, we see something like 3k to 4k nodes on the network rather then 200k+ nodes as they write in their paper... how did you get to the research? that pseudo-article in yahoo finance doesn't have a link, and the UCL centre for blockchain site is just dead https://blockchain.cs.ucl.ac.uk/ I wonder if the article even exists. The paper is at http://blockchain.cs.ucl.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/UCL_CBT_DPS_Q32021_updated-1.pdf but doesn't seem to be final. Wonder if they will fix it before full publication? Can't access that domain from here, it timesout Here is the paper Someone sent it to me I think mamy from nimbus is responding Also seems like the work has some conflict of interest.. not surprising yes, the UCL faculty is on the hedera governing council Yeah the article reads like an ad, but I'm a bit shocked that it seems like a fairly basic error to make. I'm not sure how serious peer review is in that field, but I'm afraid in mine we got to a position where besides the top say probably 10-20 journals, you can publish whatever you want in a random journal I kind of suspect in other fields like yours where money is a player, it may be worse
